title: Softr Review 2026: Features, Pros, and Cons
summary: Softr is one of the easiest no-code platforms to get a portal live with, and its ratings reflect that. The limits worth checking before you commit are app users, builders and database records.
body_markdown:
*Reviewed September 26, 2026. This is a research-based review of Softr's official pricing page and published customer feedback — not a hands-on benchmark. Jet Admin publishes this comparison and is a competing product; competitor strengths are stated as found.*


Softr is worth considering when you need a client portal or internal app over data in Airtable or a similar source, and you want it live this week. Its strongest advantage is simplicity — reviewers repeatedly call it the easiest no-code platform they have used, and a 4.7 rating across 726 G2 reviews backs that up. The trade-off is that people are metered: app users, builders and database records all carry plan limits.


This review covers what Softr builds, the limits that decide your plan, what its large review base reports, current pricing and how it compares with Jet Admin.


## Softr review: the quick verdict


Softr suits teams building portals and internal tools with a modest, countable audience, on data that already lives in a connected source. It is a weaker fit when many people need access, when your brand needs exact design control, or when you need a native mobile app.


Strong reasons to consider Softr Trade-offs to evaluate


Among the simplest no-code platforms to learn App users are capped per plan, and builders are billable


Excellent Airtable integration and fast setup Design flexibility is limited compared with Webflow-class tools


4.7 on G2 across 726 reviews, matched on Capterra Database records and workflow actions are also metered


Unlimited apps, databases, workflows and forms on every plan No native App Store or Google Play publishing


No numerical score is given, because we did not run a scored hands-on evaluation.


## What is Softr?


Softr builds client portals, internal tools and business apps on top of structured data — most commonly Airtable, though it also offers its own databases. You assemble pages from blocks, set access rules, and publish.


Its position in the category is deliberate: less design freedom than a web builder, far less learning than a general no-code platform, and a strong focus on the portal use case — customers, partners or staff logging in to see records that concern them.


Softr states it is trusted by over 1 million businesses, and lists NBA, Google, Clay, Netflix, MIT and Stripe among its customers.


## Softr's key features


### 1. Portals with role-based access


The core use case is a logged-in experience where each user sees their own records. Softr handles the authentication and visibility rules rather than requiring you to build them.


The important nuance for budgeting is that Softr distinguishes *team* users from *client* users, and both count against plan allowances. On Basic that is 5 team plus 5 client users.


### 2. Airtable integration as the default data path


Reviewers consistently single out the Airtable connection as the thing that makes Softr fast: your data model already exists, and Softr becomes the interface over it.


The qualification reviewers also report is performance — very large Airtable bases can slow the resulting app, so test at realistic data volume rather than with a sample.


### 3. Unlimited apps, databases, workflows, agents and forms


Unusually, Softr does not cap the number of apps or workflows you create, even on the free plan. What it caps is consumption: AI credits, workflow actions, database records and users.


That is a buyer-friendly structure for teams running several small apps, and it distinguishes Softr from platforms that charge per published app.


### 4. Built-in workflows and AI credits


Workflow actions are metered monthly — 500 on Free, 2,500 on Basic — and AI credits run 5, 10, 50 and 100 per month across Free, Basic, Pro and Business.


Check both against your intended automation before choosing. Softr has made AI credits a headline metric, so confirm what your specific AI usage consumes.


### 5. Forms, API and MCP access


Forms are included, with conditional logic from Basic. Softr also exposes an API and MCP access even on the free plan, which is a genuinely open stance for this category and matters if you want an AI agent to interact with your app.


## Softr pros


### It is genuinely the easiest in its class


The single most consistent theme across 726 G2 reviews is ease of use. For teams that have abandoned more capable platforms halfway through a build, that is the deciding feature — a tool people actually finish with beats a tool with a higher ceiling.


### The Airtable path removes the hardest part


If your data is already in Airtable, Softr skips data modelling entirely. Reviewers describe getting functional applications live without coding experience, which is the intended outcome and appears to be achieved reliably.


### Unlimited apps and workflows on every plan


Not charging per app is a real advantage for teams with several small portals — a department can serve three client groups without three subscriptions.


### Ratings are high and the sample is large


4.7 on G2 across 726 reviews, matched on Capterra, is strong and well-evidenced. Responsive customer support is a recurring specific in the positive feedback.


## Softr cons and limitations


### App users are capped, and builders are billable


This is the limit that most often decides the plan. The free plan allows 5 app users and up to 3 builders; Basic includes 1 builder with additional builders at $5 per month, and allows 5 team plus 5 client users.


**Who it affects:** any portal whose audience grows — which is most successful portals. **Scope:** read from Softr's pricing page for Free and Basic; Pro and Business per-plan user limits were not captured in our review and should be confirmed directly. **What to do:** forecast your user count twelve months out, not today, and price that tier rather than the entry one.


### Database records and workflow actions are metered too


Free allows 5,000 database records and 500 workflow actions a month; Basic raises those to 50,000 and 2,500.


**What to do:** check all three meters — users, records and actions — because whichever you hit first sets your plan, and it is rarely the one you were watching.


### Design flexibility is limited


Reviewers consistently note constrained customisation: limited control over views and design, forms with insufficient customisation, and less design freedom than Webflow or AI-native builders.


**Who it affects:** customer-facing portals where presentation carries brand weight. **What to do:** build one page to your brand guidelines during the free plan. This limit is immediately visible.


### No native mobile publishing, and performance strains on large bases


Reviewers report no native App Store or Google Play publishing, and that performance can slow with very large Airtable databases.


**What to evaluate:** if a store-distributed mobile app is a requirement, Softr does not provide it. And load your real record volume before committing, rather than a sample.


## What do Softr users say?


Source Rating Reviews behind it


[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/softr/reviews) 4.7 / 5 726


[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/232331/Softr/reviews/) 4.7 / 5 Not verified


**Positive themes:** ease of use above all; seamless Airtable integration; speed to a functional app without coding; intuitive interface; responsive customer support.


**Negative themes:** limited customisation and design flexibility; form customisation constraints; no native mobile publishing; performance on very large databases; features requiring higher plans.


This is an unusually consistent review profile. Nobody complains that Softr is hard or unreliable; the complaints are all about ceilings. That is a good sign for adoption and a clear instruction for evaluation — test the ceilings, not the basics.

### When Softr is the better choice


If your data is in Airtable, your audience is small and countable, and you want a portal live in days, Softr is very hard to beat — and its ease-of-use advantage is real rather than marketing. A 4.7 across 726 reviews is not an accident.


## Who should use Softr — and who should compare alternatives?


**Good fit:** Airtable-backed client portals; small internal tools; teams with one or two builders and a bounded user list; anyone who has struggled to finish a build on a more complex platform.


**Compare alternatives if:** your portal audience will grow past the plan's user caps; your data belongs in a database rather than a spreadsheet-style source; you need exact brand control or native mobile distribution; or several colleagues need to build simultaneously.


If the constraint turns out to be the number of people who need access,[build the same portal on your existing data with Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/) and compare the totals at your real user count.


## Softr review FAQ


### What is Softr?


A no-code platform for building client portals, internal tools and business apps on top of Airtable or its own databases, with authentication and access rules included.


### Is Softr free?


Yes — a free plan with 5 AI credits a month, up to 3 builders, 5 app users, 5,000 database records and 500 workflow actions a month, plus unlimited apps and workflows. Basic is $19 a month billed yearly.


### How many users can a Softr app have?


App users are capped by plan: 5 on Free, and 5 team plus 5 client users on Basic. Confirm Pro and Business allowances directly, as those rows were not captured in our review.


### Does Softr charge per builder?


Basic includes one builder, with additional builders at $5 per month. The free plan allows up to three.


### Can Softr publish a native mobile app?


Reviewers report no native App Store or Google Play publishing. Confirm whether a web app is acceptable for your users.


### How does Softr compare with Jet Admin?


Both build portals without code. Softr is faster if your data is in Airtable and your audience is small; Jet Admin connects to databases and APIs directly and includes unlimited users on every plan. Audience size is usually the deciding factor.


## Price by audience, not by data


The most useful thing to do before choosing a Softr plan is to count the people who will log in over the next year, separate them into team and client, and add up the builders. That number chooses your tier far more often than records or features do.


If it lands above what the plan comfortably allows,[build the same portal on your own data with Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/) and compare both at that user count rather than at launch.
